question.text: In an AC circuit, the instantaneous values of emf and current are Ε=200sin300t V and  i=2sin⁡300t+π3  A respectively. The average power consumed (in watt) is

solution.text:
The average power consumed in an AC circuit is given by

P=V0I02cos⁡ϕ

Where ϕ is phase angle and V0 and I0 are the peak values of voltage and current respectively.

Given, V0=200 V, I0=2 A, ϕ=π3.

P=200×22cos⁡π3

=200×22×12=100 W

It is found that the maximum value of <math> <mtext>Q</mtext> </math> is <math> <mrow> <mtext>200</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>μ</mi><mtext>C</mtext><mtext>.</mtext></mrow> </math> When <math> <mrow> <mtext>Q</mtext><mo>=</mo><mtext>100</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi>μ</mi><mtext>C,</mtext></mrow> </math> what is the value of <math> <mrow> <mfenced close="|" open="|" separators=","> <mrow> <mtext>dI</mtext> <mo>/</mo> <mtext>dt</mtext></mrow></mfenced></mrow></math>?

solution.text:
This is a problem of L - C oscillations.
Charge stored in the capacitor oscillates simple harmonically as

Q= Q 0 sin( ωt±ϕ )
 
Here, Q 0 = maximum value of Q=200  μC=2× 10 −4   C
 
ω = 1 LC = 1 2 × 10 - 3 5.0 × 1 0 - 6 = 10 4  s -1
 
At   t=0,  Q= Q 0 then
 
Q( t )= Q 0 cosωt                               ... (i)
 
I t = dQ dt = - Q 0 ω sin ω t           and             ... (ii)
 
dI t dt = - Q 0 ω 2 cos ω t                         ... (iii)
 
Q=100  μC or Q 0 2

cos ω t = 1 2    or   ω t = π 3

dI dt = 2.0 × 1 0 - 4 C 1 0 4 s -1 2 1 2
 
dI dt = 1 0000  A / s

question.text: An <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>AC</mi></math> circuit drawing power from a source of angular frequency <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi>rad</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> has a power factor of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>0.6</mtext></math>. In this condition, a resistance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is present and the current is lagging behind the voltage. If a capacitor is connected in series, then the required capacitance that will result in a power factor of unity is

solution.text:
As the current lags the voltage, the circuit must contain a combination of resistance and inductance.

Power factor cos⁡ϕ=0.6

⇒RR2+XL2=0.6

⇒R2+XL2=R0.62

⇒XL2=R20.62-R2

⇒XL2=R2×0.640.36

∴XL=0.8 R0.6=4R3

Now we want the power factor cos⁡ϕ=1

This is the condition of resonance in which

XL=XC

∴XC=4R3

⇒1ωC=4R3

⇒C=34×50×100=150 μF
